title: The 1967 ulcer and his drinking
summary: He gets an ulcer when work dries up in California, recovers within weeks to tour England, and says the doctor was wrong that he could never drink again.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: I want to go back to what is the real sore subject with you and that is 1967 when you got sick and I think that you got sick because you didn't have any work.
Well, that was out in California--
Yeah.
That's when I moved out there.
Well, I suppose that had a lot to do with it; I got an ulcer --- and they say if you worry a lot and I am a worrier -- my wife can tell you that---
So can I tell you that---
Yeah - I am sort of a worrier but I suppose that had a hell of a lot to do with the ulcer I got and, uh, ---
People were writing you off---
Well, several writers wrote me off but, uh, I didn't---
But, three weeks after you got sick you were back playing.

I was playing in Europe - I toured England again. So-- and I can remember the guy saying to me -- I think my wife had something to do with this - she and the doctor -- trying to con me out of drinking and they said - you can't drink anymore in your lifetime - you know - (laughter)---
That didn't quite hold--
No, but anyway, I drank for the last --- what--
Twenty years---
Twenty years since they said I couldn't drink but I don't---
It's been twelve years since you were sick and you look and act better now and play just as well.

Yeah - well, I don't drink as much; let's put it like that. I don't really drink as much. And, uh, I space my drinking -- during my practice period before I go on the stage - I always have three or four drinks before I go on the stage; that does me just fine.
There are, of course, legendary stories about the drinking that went on in Condon's and you were right in the center of it ---
Well, I suppose when I look back, I think I was the biggest drinker but it didn't affect me as much as it did some others.
Yeah.
I seem just to blow it off somehow - you know.
I don't know how it happened but it killed a lot of guys, but here you are.

Yeah - I'm still here. So, I think that doctor sure was wrong as hell---(end of Tape 2) (beginning of Tape 3 - Side One)---) --the Eddie Condon's uptown and I decided about this time that maybe I should move around. So, I had many, many bands and worked many, many places and it seemed as though our kind of music was sort of sliding down hill.
